title: AWS launches Local Zone Edge location in Bogotá, Colombia
html:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) has launched a new Local Zone Edge cloud location in Bogotá, Colombia.

“Today, AWS announces the general availability of a new Local Zone in Bogotá, Colombia, bringing AWS infrastructure closer to end users for applications that require single-digit millisecond latency,” the company said. “You can use the Bogotá Local Zone for workloads such as real-time gaming, live video streaming, medical imaging, and financial transaction processing.”

Local Zones act as Edge locations to host applications that require low latency to end-users or on-premises installations. Each zone offers select services (compute, storage, database, etc.) close to population centers for latency-sensitive applications, often where Amazon doesn't have an existing data center footprint.

As with all the company’s Local Zones in Latin America, the parent cloud region of the Bogotá Local Zone is US East in Northern Virginia.

Local Zones were first launched in 2019 in the US. AWS has since launched more than 30 Local Zones in international markets across North America, Europe, Latin America, Africa, and APAC.

AWS has previously told DCD that Local Zones can be hosted in third-party data centers, but can also be hosted in Amazon-owned facilities that are not part of a geographic cloud region.

This year has seen Amazon launch a Local Zone in Istanbul, Turkey; Hanoi, Vietnam; Athens, Greece; and Las Vegas, Nevada.
summary: Company continues roll-out of smaller Edge zones
